newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms Siemens ratings, outlook.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Siemens ratings, outlook.

text.p: LONDON, March 10 - Standard & Poor's today has affirmed its triple-A' senior unsecured and A-1'-plus commercial paper ratings of Siemens AG and guaranteed related entities (see list below). The stable outlook is also affirmed.
The ratings on Germany-based Siemens AG and its guaranteed subsidiaries reflect the group's exceptional financial strength and the portfolio effect of its diversified business units.

Siemens is one of the largest and most diversified suppliers of electronic and electrical products in the world, with operations covering a variety off sectors, including infrastructure, industrial, information technology, medical and lighting.

The profitability of the main divisions within the portfolio has become slightly more balanced in recent years, as negative trends in the telecommunications equipment and power generation operations have been offset by a recovery in information technology and semiconductors.

As such, profitability in 1996 was to a large extent dependent on an upturn in the cyclical semiconductor industry. Sales are predominantly in Europe, though expansion in the U.S. and Asia Pacific in recent years continues to further improve the group's geographic spread and growth prospects.
Although the breadth of Siemens' operations produces a high degree of cash flow stability, reported operating margins remain low relative to major competitors.
Management's efforts to improve profitability are ongoing, and the group continues its restructuring efforts in order to improve productivity.

However, as a significant share of foreign sales continue to be served out of the German production base, productivity improvements will likely be partially offset by increased wages, placing Siemens in a challenging competitive operating position.
Siemens continues to be highly liquid. Liquid assets exceeded total debt excluding pension provisions by DM16 billion (about US$10 billion) at year-end Sept. 30th, 1996.
The group's strong cash flow is, in the absence of major acquisitions, generally more than sufficient to fund group working capital and capital expenditures.
In fiscal year 1996, income before taxes (excluding extraordinary items) rose by 20% to DM2.5 billion, on sales up 5% to DM91.4 billion.
In the first quarter to Dec. 31, 1996, net income declined by 5%, on sales up 6% at DM20.9 billion reflecting the sharp price decline of semiconductor memory chips.

Early in 1997 Siemens announced the acquisitions of AEG Electrocom from Daimler Benz and Electrowatt's industrial unit. The first acquisition will strengthen Siemens first tier position in Automation.

The second will improve its competitive position in Industrial and Building systems, which in 1996 reported a pre-tax loss of DM102 million. The integration of these investments should be concluded by 1997/1998, with profits contributing from 1997/1998 onwards.

As the funding of these acquisitions will be partially covered by disposals, Siemens financial strength continues to remain adequate for the current ratings, assuming no additional, sizable acquisitions in the near future.
Profits before extraordinary items for the full year 1997 are expected to remain on the level of 1996.
OUTLOOK: Stable.

Siemens faces major challenges in further improving profitability, and several of its units continue to be under increased competitive and price pressures. The combination of the group's strong market positions, management's commitment to productivity gains, and its financial resources are expected to continue to support the ratings, absent any significant cash-financed acquisitions in the near term, Standard & Poor's said.
